name.text: Alternate Segment and Angle at Centre (INNODEMS)

questiontext.text:
In the diagram, \(O\) is the centre of the circle and \(PT\) is the tangent to the circle at \(T\). The chord \(TQ\) subtends an angle of \( {@theta@}^\circ \) at the centre, that is \( \angle TOQ = {@theta@}^\circ \).

[[jsxgraph width="460px" height="460px"]] var theta = {#theta#}; // central angle TOQ (degrees), from question variables var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-3.3, 3.2, 3.3, -3.4], keepaspectratio: true, axis: false, showCopyright: false, showNavigation: false }); var R = 2.5; var rad = Math.PI / 180; var O = board.create('point', [0, 0], {name: 'O', size: 2, fixed: true, fillColor: '#333', strokeColor: '#333', label: {offset: [8, 8]}}); var Tang = 270 * rad; var T = board.create('point', [R * Math.cos(Tang), R * Math.sin(Tang)], {name: 'T', size: 3, fixed: true, fillColor: '#1565c0', strokeColor: '#1565c0', label: {offset: [0, -14], anchorX: 'middle', anchorY: 'top'}}); var Qang = (270 + theta) * rad; var Q = board.create('point', [R * Math.cos(Qang), R * Math.sin(Qang)], {name: 'Q', size: 3, fixed: true, fillColor: '#1565c0', strokeColor: '#1565c0', label: {offset: [12, 0], anchorX: 'left', anchorY: 'middle'}}); Find \( \angle PTQ \), giving your answer in degrees: \( \angle PTQ = \) [[input:ans1]]\(^\circ\) [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Use the Alternate Segment Theorem: the angle between the tangent \(PT\) and the chord \(TQ\) equals the angle that the chord subtends in the alternate segment, namely \( \angle TSQ \).

The angle at the circumference is half the angle at the centre standing on the same chord \(TQ\), so

\[ \angle TSQ = \tfrac{1}{2}\,\angle TOQ = \tfrac{1}{2}\times {@theta@}^\circ = {@ta1@}^\circ . \]

Therefore

\[ \angle PTQ = \angle TSQ = {@ta1@}^\circ . \]

(Check, via triangle \(OTQ\): it is isosceles with \(OT = OQ\), so \( \angle OTQ = \tfrac{1}{2}(180^\circ - {@theta@}^\circ) = {@wrong_baseang@}^\circ\). The radius meets the tangent at \(90^\circ\), so \( \angle PTQ = 90^\circ - {@wrong_baseang@}^\circ = {@ta1@}^\circ\), as expected.)

node.description: Misconception: gave the central angle (forgot to halve).

truefeedback.text: That is the central angle \( \angle TOQ \). The tangent-chord angle equals the angle in the alternate segment, which is half the central angle — so divide by \(2\).

node.description: Misconception: gave angle OTQ (isosceles base angle) instead of PTQ.

truefeedback.text: That is \( \angle OTQ \), a base angle of the isosceles triangle \(OTQ\). The angle you want is \( \angle PTQ = 90^\circ - \angle OTQ \), since the radius \(OT\) meets the tangent at \(90^\circ\). (Equivalently, use the Alternate Segment Theorem directly.)

node.description: Misconception: doubled the central angle instead of halving it.

truefeedback.text: You doubled the central angle. It is the other way round: the tangent-chord angle is half the central angle \( \angle TOQ \), so you should divide by \(2\), not multiply.

falsefeedback.text: Not correct. Hint: the tangent-chord angle \( \angle PTQ \) equals the inscribed angle in the alternate segment, which is half the central angle \( \angle TOQ \). See the worked solution.
